newsitem.title: USA: Playboy int'l, entertainment groups improve.
newsitem.headline: Playboy int'l, entertainment groups improve.

text.p: Playboy Enterprises Inc, which earlier reported slightly higher first-quarter results, said Thursday its entertainment group and international publishing and product marketing operations performed well in the quarter.
Playboy earlier said it earned $1.037 million, or $0.05 a share, in the quarter versus $1.012 million, or $0.05, during the same period last year.

Net income, adjusted to eliminate federal income tax expense that will not be paid because of net operating loss carryforwards, was $1.7 million, or $.08 per share, compared to $1.0 million, or $0.05 per share, Playboy said.

The company's Publishing Group's operating income fell to $1.1 million from $2.8 million, due to a drop in Playboy magazine's ad pages, increased production costs, including higher paper prices, and the mix of newsstand specials.

Revenues for the Group were down 2 percent to $32.1 million. International publishing revenues were up, reflecting Playboy's acquisition late in 1996 of an additional 45 percent interest in the Polish edition of Playboy Entertainment.

Its entertainment group's operating income almost tripled in the first quarter to $3.5 million from $1.2 million, driven by higher satellite direct-to-home revenues, increased international sales and the one-year-old AdulTVision network reporting its first quarter of profitability, Playboy said.
